general.title: What is Forge?
general.answer: Forge is the Chrysasynth browser-based audio workspace. Open an instrument from All Tools to explore synths, sequencing, sound design, effects and utilities.

general.title: How do I open another tool?
general.answer: Select All Tools in the left sidebar, then choose the instrument you want to open. You can return to the library without leaving Forge.
keywords: how do i open another tool?

general.title: Where do my imported files go?
general.answer: Most Forge instruments process imported audio locally in the browser, but saving and export differ by tool. Use its Export or Record function before closing a session.
keywords: where do my imported files go?

general.title: Why is there no sound?
general.answer: Check your output and volume, then press Play or enable audio inside the instrument. Browsers usually require a click before starting audio. If a tool uses an online library, it may also need an internet connection.

general.title: How do I export my music?
general.answer: Export options depend on the instrument. Some render WAV, others record WebM or export MIDI, and some are designed for live exploration. Open a tool and ask about its export controls.
keywords: how do i export my music?

general.title: Can I send feedback?
general.answer: Use Feedback / Bug below. Sending is available only after the feedback backend is connected. The form will tell you whether it can submit.

general.title: How can I find a creative starting point?
general.answer: Choose a musical aim first: a beat, harmony, texture or transition. SUBDIVE explores bass grooves, Chord Bloom explores harmony, Granular Pad explores textures, and CLIMAX designs rises.
keywords: how can i find a creative starting point?

general.title: Which tool should I use for a bassline?
general.answer: Try SUBDIVE for generated bass patterns or AXIS for a step-sequenced acid-style phrase. Knot offers a playable synthesizer if you prefer to perform notes yourself.
keywords: which tool should i use for a bassline?

general.title: Which tool should I use for chords?
general.answer: Try Chord Bloom to generate progressions, Nodes for chord-based arpeggios, or Structura to place harmonic material in an arrangement.
keywords: which tool should i use for chords?

general.title: Which tool should I use for ambient textures?
general.answer: Try Granular Pad for stretched audio grains, Aura Sampler for reshaped samples, pixelTone for image-derived textures, or Mindshift for interactive audiovisual exploration.
keywords: which tool should i use for ambient textures?

general.title: How can I build tension in a track?
general.answer: Raise density, brightness or rhythmic activity gradually, then introduce contrast at the transition. Structura can outline the arrangement, CLIMAX can design a riser, and Shepard can provide an endless-rise illusion.
keywords: how can i build tension in a track?

general.title: What is the Dorian mode?
general.answer: Dorian is a minor-sounding scale with a raised sixth compared with natural minor. D Dorian contains D E F G A B C. It is useful for grooves that feel minor but not as dark as Aeolian.

general.title: What is an arpeggio?
general.answer: An arpeggio plays the notes of a chord one after another rather than all at once. Try Nodes or Duality Synth to explore changing arpeggio patterns.

general.title: What is a polyrhythm?
general.answer: A polyrhythm layers different rhythmic subdivisions over a shared time span, such as three hits against four. Polyrhythm Bouncer makes this audible and visible; Kaleidoscope Studio lets you arrange several parts.

general.title: How does a filter cutoff work?
general.answer: Cutoff sets the boundary region a filter emphasizes or attenuates. On a low-pass filter, lowering cutoff generally removes brightness; Resonance boosts energy near the cutoff point.
keywords: how does a filter cutoff work?

general.title: What does reverb do?
general.answer: Reverb simulates reflections and decay in a space, from a small room to a large hall. Use the Reverb instrument to compare spatial presets and shape decay, damping and pre-delay.

5th-essence.summary: 5TH Essence is a modular audio effects rack. Combine Air (filters), Fire (saturation), Water (modulation), Earth (reverb) and Aether (spectral texture) in any order.
5th-essence.capabilities: 5TH Essence is a modular audio effects rack. Combine Air (filters), Fire (saturation), Water (modulation), Earth (reverb) and Aether (spectral texture) in any order. Choose a question below for first steps, specific controls or a creative idea.

faq.title: What is 5TH Essence?
faq.answer: 5TH Essence is a modular audio effects rack. Combine Air (filters), Fire (saturation), Water (modulation), Earth (reverb) and Aether (spectral texture) in any order.

faq.title: How do I start?
faq.answer: Drop in an audio file or select Try demo. Add a module, choose its mode and adjust its controls. Drag the modules to change their processing order, then preview the chain.

faq.title: Give me a creative idea
faq.answer: Turn a plain synth note into a shifting atmosphere: add Fire for gentle saturation, Water for slow chorus, then Earth for a long space. Move Earth earlier in the chain to hear how order changes the texture.

faq.title: Can I change the effect order?
faq.answer: Yes. Drag module cards to rearrange the serial effects chain, or use the accessible arrow controls. An effect placed before saturation will sound different from one placed after it.
keywords: can i change the effect order?

faq.title: How do I export my effects chain?
faq.answer: When the preview sounds right, choose Export WAV. 5TH Essence renders a stereo 16-bit WAV, including an effect tail. The exported audio reflects the current module order and settings.
keywords: how do i export my effects chain?

aura-sampler.summary: Aura Sampler turns imported audio into a playable sample instrument. Change pitch, shape envelopes and modulation, and add delay or reverb to create new textures.
aura-sampler.capabilities: Aura Sampler turns imported audio into a playable sample instrument. Change pitch, shape envelopes and modulation, and add delay or reverb to create new textures. Choose a question below for first steps, specific controls or a creative idea.

faq.title: What is Aura Sampler?
faq.answer: Aura Sampler turns imported audio into a playable sample instrument. Change pitch, shape envelopes and modulation, and add delay or reverb to create new textures.

faq.title: How do I start?
faq.answer: Click Load sample or drag an audio file into the workspace. Press Preview or play a note on the chromatic keyboard. Try Fray, Veil or Rift, then explore Shape, Motion and Space.

faq.title: Give me a creative idea
faq.answer: Import a short vocal or instrumental fragment. Enable Loop, set a slow LFO and add Space processing. Try Reverse for an airy, evolving bed, then record a phrase you like.

faq.title: What are Fray, Veil and Rift?
faq.answer: They are texture presets, not separate export formats. Use them as starting points, then fine-tune Shape for tone, Motion for envelopes and LFO, and Space for delay and reverb.
keywords: what are fray, veil and rift?

faq.title: How do I record my sampler performance?
faq.answer: Load a sample and select your settings, then start Record. Play notes or Preview, stop recording and save the resulting WAV. Recording depends on browser audio-capture support.
keywords: how do i record my sampler performance?

faq.title: What effects are included?
faq.answer: Fray, Veil and Rift are texture starting points (seeds), not the only effects. Use Shape for texture and tone, Motion for envelopes and LFO, and Space for delay and reverb.

faq.title: Can I record audio?
faq.answer: After loading and playing a sample, click Record WAV in the Capture & Output section. AURA records its output as a 16-bit WAV, for up to 60 seconds.

axis.summary: AXIS is a scale-aware melodic 16-step sequencer with synth controls, accents, slides, A/B patterns and a drum accompaniment.
axis.capabilities: AXIS is a scale-aware melodic 16-step sequencer with synth controls, accents, slides, A/B patterns and a drum accompaniment. Choose a question below for first steps, specific controls or a creative idea.

faq.title: What is AXIS?
faq.answer: AXIS is a scale-aware melodic 16-step sequencer with synth controls, accents, slides, A/B patterns and a drum accompaniment.

faq.title: How do I start?
faq.answer: Choose a Seed, root note and scale. Edit the 16-step melodic grid, press Play and adjust the AXIS VOICE sound. You can add accents or slides to individual steps.

faq.title: Give me a creative idea
faq.answer: Try Serpent Acid in a minor scale. Put accents on a few offbeats, add slides between notes and slowly adjust cutoff and resonance for a growing acid-style phrase.

faq.title: How do A/B patterns work?
faq.answer: Edit two variations of your sequence and use the A/B chaining controls to alternate between them. A subtle change in the second pattern can make a short loop feel much longer.

faq.title: Can I record an AXIS sequence?
faq.answer: Yes, AXIS includes recording controls. Start playback, record the passage you want and stop to save it. The available recorded format follows the implementation and your browser.
keywords: can i record an axis sequence?

binaural-beats.summary: Binaural Beats plays slightly different tones in the left and right channels. With stereo headphones, the difference can be perceived as a rhythmic beat.
binaural-beats.capabilities: Binaural Beats plays slightly different tones in the left and right channels. With stereo headphones, the difference can be perceived as a rhythmic beat. Choose a question below for first steps, specific controls or a creative idea.

faq.title: What is Binaural Beats?
faq.answer: Binaural Beats plays slightly different tones in the left and right channels. With stereo headphones, the difference can be perceived as a rhythmic beat.

faq.title: How do I start?
faq.answer: Put on stereo headphones, select a carrier frequency and beat difference, then press Play. Keep the volume comfortable and set the session timer if needed.

faq.title: Give me a creative idea
faq.answer: For a minimal listening texture, choose a low listening level, a gentle waveform and a little pink noise. Let the sound stay simple instead of stacking many elements.

faq.title: Why should I use headphones?
faq.answer: Binaural playback sends different tones to the left and right ears. Stereo headphones keep those channels separate. The numerical presets are audio examples, not guaranteed health outcomes.

faq.title: Can I add background noise?
faq.answer: Yes. The generator includes a pink-noise layer you can mix quietly with the two tones. It starts disabled, so turn it on only if you want the added texture.

bpm-milliseconds.summary: BPM ⇆ Milliseconds converts tempo into timing values for delays, LFOs and tempo-synchronized effects. It also converts milliseconds back into BPM.
bpm-milliseconds.capabilities: BPM ⇆ Milliseconds converts tempo into timing values for delays, LFOs and tempo-synchronized effects. It also converts milliseconds back into BPM. Choose a question below for first steps, specific controls or a creative idea.

faq.title: What is BPM ⇆ Milliseconds?
faq.answer: BPM ⇆ Milliseconds converts tempo into timing values for delays, LFOs and tempo-synchronized effects. It also converts milliseconds back into BPM.

faq.title: How do I start?
faq.answer: Enter a BPM value, choose a rhythmic division and select Straight, Dotted or Triplet timing. The matching milliseconds are calculated automatically.

faq.title: Give me a creative idea
faq.answer: Try a dotted eighth-note delay instead of a straight quarter note. The echoes land between the main beats and create a more propulsive rhythmic pattern.

faq.title: How do dotted and triplet values work?
faq.answer: Dotted timing lasts 1.5 times a straight note; triplet timing lasts two-thirds of it. Select the note division and timing style to get the exact value for your tempo.
keywords: how do dotted and triplet values work?

faq.title: Can I tap a tempo here?
faq.answer: Yes. Tap the tempo button at least twice, or use Space outside input fields. The utility estimates BPM from your taps; you can copy the calculated milliseconds.
keywords: can i tap a tempo here?

brth4.summary: BRTH4 is a visual breathing guide with Box, Relax, Focus and Custom patterns, a session timer and optional sound textures.
brth4.capabilities: BRTH4 is a visual breathing guide with Box, Relax, Focus and Custom patterns, a session timer and optional sound textures. Choose a question below for first steps, specific controls or a creative idea.

faq.title: What is BRTH4?
faq.answer: BRTH4 is a visual breathing guide with Box, Relax, Focus and Custom patterns, a session timer and optional sound textures.

faq.title: How do I start?
faq.answer: Choose a breathing pattern, set a session duration and press Start Session. Follow the moving marker around the square; sound is optional and starts off.

faq.title: Give me a creative idea
faq.answer: Try a short Box session without sound, then repeat with low-volume brown noise. Notice whether following the visual rhythm changes how you engage with the session.

faq.title: What breathing patterns are available?
faq.answer: Box uses 4–4–4–4; Relax uses 4–7–8; Focus uses 5–5–5–5. Custom lets you edit the phases yourself. Choose a comfortable pattern rather than forcing a long hold.

faq.title: Can I use BRTH4 without audio?
faq.answer: Yes. The visual breathing guide works silently by default. If you enable brown noise or binaural tones, keep volume comfortable and use headphones for binaural separation.
keywords: can i use brth4 without audio?

chord-bloom.summary: Chord Bloom generates chord progressions with keys, scales, mood seeds, optional seventh chords and playable synth sounds.
chord-bloom.capabilities: Chord Bloom generates chord progressions with keys, scales, mood seeds, optional seventh chords and playable synth sounds. Choose a question below for first steps, specific controls or a creative idea.

faq.title: What is Chord Bloom?
faq.answer: Chord Bloom generates chord progressions with keys, scales, mood seeds, optional seventh chords and playable synth sounds.

faq.title: How do I start?
faq.answer: Select a key, scale and mood seed, then click Generate. Press Play to audition the chords; refine BPM, strum and synth character to shape the progression.

faq.title: Give me a creative idea
faq.answer: Explore a Lydian progression with a gentle pad, slow strumming and reverb. Keep the bass simple and let the upper chord tones create an airy harmonic feel.

faq.title: Can I use seventh chords?
faq.answer: Yes. Enable seventh chords to add harmonic color to generated progressions. Try comparing the same seed with and without sevenths before changing the synthesizer sound.

faq.title: Can I export my chord progression?
faq.answer: Yes. Chord Bloom supports MIDI export, so you can move the progression into another music application. It also includes audio recording and sharing features.
keywords: can i export my chord progression?

chorus-flanger.summary: Chorus / Flanger adds time-based modulation to audio. Chorus creates layered width and movement; flanger produces sweeping comb-filter resonances.
chorus-flanger.capabilities: Chorus / Flanger adds time-based modulation to audio. Chorus creates layered width and movement; flanger produces sweeping comb-filter resonances. Choose a question below for first steps, specific controls or a creative idea.

faq.title: What is Chorus Flanger?
faq.answer: Chorus / Flanger adds time-based modulation to audio. Chorus creates layered width and movement; flanger produces sweeping comb-filter resonances.

faq.title: How do I start?
faq.answer: Load an audio file or use the demo, press Play and choose Chorus or Flanger. Adjust Rate, Depth, Feedback and Mix while listening.

faq.title: Give me a creative idea
faq.answer: For a wide synth pad, start with Chorus, use a slow Rate and modest Depth, then blend with Mix. Compare the sound in stereo before raising Feedback.

faq.title: What is the difference between chorus and flanger?
faq.answer: Chorus uses moving delay/pitch differences for a thicker sound. Flanger uses a very short, modulated delay, creating pronounced notches and a sweeping jet-like character.
keywords: what is the difference between chorus and flanger?

faq.title: Can I save the processed sound?
faq.answer: Use the tool’s WAV export after adjusting the effect. The exported result contains the processed audio rather than just a preset setting.
keywords: can i save the processed sound?

climax.summary: CLIMAX designs risers and transitions from imported WAV audio using automated volume, filtering, pitch, reverb or speed.
climax.capabilities: CLIMAX designs risers and transitions from imported WAV audio using automated volume, filtering, pitch, reverb or speed. Choose a question below for first steps, specific controls or a creative idea.

faq.title: What is CLIMAX?
faq.answer: CLIMAX designs risers and transitions from imported WAV audio using automated volume, filtering, pitch, reverb or speed.

faq.title: How do I start?
faq.answer: Import a WAV clip, choose the automation type, set Intensity and Shape, then preview the transition. Export WAV when it fits the arrangement.

faq.title: Give me a creative idea
faq.answer: Make an eight-bar build from a noise texture: choose Filter automation and an eased-exponential curve, then increase intensity so the brightness accelerates toward the drop.

faq.title: What can I automate?
faq.answer: CLIMAX can automate volume, filter, pitch, reverb or speed. Linear and eased-exponential envelopes provide different build shapes. Pitch and speed effects behave like tape playback.

faq.title: Does the riser export as WAV?
faq.answer: Yes. Use Export WAV to render the current automation. Reverb tails are contained within the source duration, and speed or pitch transformations may loop non-loopable material.
keywords: does the riser export as wav?

cosmic-garden.summary: Cosmic Garden is an interactive audiovisual garden where musical scales shape a growing 3D scene. Clicking seeds triggers harmonic sounds.
cosmic-garden.capabilities: Cosmic Garden is an interactive audiovisual garden where musical scales shape a growing 3D scene. Clicking seeds triggers harmonic sounds. Choose a question below for first steps, specific controls or a creative idea.

faq.title: What is Cosmic Garden?
faq.answer: Cosmic Garden is an interactive audiovisual garden where musical scales shape a growing 3D scene. Clicking seeds triggers harmonic sounds.

faq.title: How do I start?
faq.answer: Choose a musical scale such as Dorian, Lydian or Minor. Click the visual seeds to play chords; drag to orbit the garden and scroll to zoom.

faq.title: Give me a creative idea
faq.answer: Choose Dorian, explore a few seed combinations slowly and leave pauses between them. Record the sequence as a drifting harmonic sketch you could later layer beneath a track.

faq.title: How do the scales affect the garden?
faq.answer: The selected scale guides the harmonic notes assigned to the interactive seeds. Switch scales to hear how the same style of gestures leads to a different musical atmosphere.
keywords: how do the scales affect the garden?

faq.title: Can I record the garden?
faq.answer: Yes. Cosmic Garden includes WAV recording. Start capture, perform a short sequence of seed interactions and stop to save the audio.

delay.summary: Delay adds rhythmic echoes to audio, including stereo and ping-pong routing, tempo sync, feedback, damping and character controls.
delay.capabilities: Delay adds rhythmic echoes to audio, including stereo and ping-pong routing, tempo sync, feedback, damping and character controls. Choose a question below for first steps, specific controls or a creative idea.

faq.title: What is Delay?
faq.answer: Delay adds rhythmic echoes to audio, including stereo and ping-pong routing, tempo sync, feedback, damping and character controls.

faq.title: How do I start?
faq.answer: Import a file or choose the demo guitar phrase, then press Play. Choose a preset and adjust Time, Feedback and Mix to hear the changes.

faq.title: Give me a creative idea
faq.answer: Enable Ping-Pong and select a dotted eighth-note division with Tempo Sync. Lower Feedback for a tight groove or raise it for a longer stereo echo pattern.

faq.title: How does tempo sync work?
faq.answer: Set BPM and a rhythmic note division to align echoes with the beat. If you drag the Time control while synced, the tool can switch to free milliseconds for manual timing.

faq.title: Can I export echoes with their tails?
faq.answer: Yes. Export WAV uses offline processing and includes a calculated echo tail. Very long feedback settings can make that tail noticeably longer.
keywords: can i export echoes with their tails?

duality-synth.summary: Duality Synth is a 16-step arpeggiator blending two synth characters, A and B, through an interactive Morph Ring.
duality-synth.capabilities: Duality Synth is a 16-step arpeggiator blending two synth characters, A and B, through an interactive Morph Ring. Choose a question below for first steps, specific controls or a creative idea.

faq.title: What is Duality Synth?
faq.answer: Duality Synth is a 16-step arpeggiator blending two synth characters, A and B, through an interactive Morph Ring.

faq.title: How do I start?
faq.answer: Choose a Morph Seed, root, scale and BPM. Press Play and edit the 16 steps. Drag the Morph Ring to hear the blend between the two characters.

faq.title: Give me a creative idea
faq.answer: Make a repeating minor arpeggio, start close to sound A and enable Orbit at a slow speed. Let the timbre drift toward B while the notes remain stable.

faq.title: What does Orbit do?
faq.answer: Orbit automatically moves the morph position between the A and B sound characters. Adjust Orbit Speed to control how quickly the timbre changes.

faq.title: How does the Morph Ring work?
faq.answer: The top of the ring selects A; the bottom selects B. Either side is a roughly 50/50 blend. The ring crossfades between two separate synth and effect voices.
keywords: how does the morph ring work?

faq.title: How do I record and export a WAV?
faq.answer: Start Play, click Record, then Stop Rec when you have captured the passage. Choose Export WAV to save a 16-bit stereo PCM file. Browser capture and decoding support are required.

etheremin.summary: Etheremin is a camera-based gesture synthesizer inspired by the theremin, letting hand movements control pitch and expression.
etheremin.capabilities: Etheremin is a camera-based gesture synthesizer inspired by the theremin, letting hand movements control pitch and expression. Choose a question below for first steps, specific controls or a creative idea.

faq.title: What is Etheremin?
faq.answer: Etheremin is a camera-based gesture synthesizer inspired by the theremin, letting hand movements control pitch and expression.

faq.title: How do I start?
faq.answer: Click Start Playing, permit camera access and move your hand through the camera view. Horizontal motion controls pitch; vertical movement affects expression.

faq.title: Give me a creative idea
faq.answer: Choose a voice like Vocal Theremin, use a minor scale and slow gliding movements between notes. Add gentle vibrato for an expressive, floating lead.

faq.title: How do the hand gestures control sound?
faq.answer: Etheremin tracks your hand through the webcam. Moving sideways changes pitch, while vertical motion shapes expression. Good light and a clear camera view help tracking.
keywords: how do the hand gestures control sound?

faq.title: Do I need a webcam?
faq.answer: Yes, for gesture control. Allow camera access in your browser and make sure no other application is preventing the camera from being used.

fibonacci-melody.summary: Fibonacci Melody creates musical sequences from Fibonacci-inspired number patterns, rhythmic durations and selected scales.
fibonacci-melody.capabilities: Fibonacci Melody creates musical sequences from Fibonacci-inspired number patterns, rhythmic durations and selected scales. Choose a question below for first steps, specific controls or a creative idea.

faq.title: What is Fibonacci Melody?
faq.answer: Fibonacci Melody creates musical sequences from Fibonacci-inspired number patterns, rhythmic durations and selected scales.

faq.title: How do I start?
faq.answer: Choose a key, scale, step count and rhythm model. Press Play to hear the sequence, and inspect it in the Geometry or Piano Roll view.

faq.title: Give me a creative idea
faq.answer: Try a pentatonic scale with Fibonacci Durations instead of even eighth notes. The irregular spacing can become the start of an unusual melodic hook.

faq.title: What are Fibonacci Durations?
faq.answer: They use Fibonacci-inspired values to vary note lengths. Compare the result against the regular rhythm option to hear how the same pitch sequence changes character.

faq.title: Can I export the melody?
faq.answer: Yes. Export MIDI to move the generated notes into your DAW, where you can revoice them with other instruments.

frequency-note.summary: Frequency ⇆ Note finds the nearest equal-tempered musical note for a frequency and shows how many cents it differs from the note reference.
frequency-note.capabilities: Frequency ⇆ Note finds the nearest equal-tempered musical note for a frequency and shows how many cents it differs from the note reference. Choose a question below for first steps, specific controls or a creative idea.

faq.title: What is Frequency ⇆ Note?
faq.answer: Frequency ⇆ Note finds the nearest equal-tempered musical note for a frequency and shows how many cents it differs from the note reference.

faq.title: How do I start?
faq.answer: Enter a frequency in hertz. The tool identifies the closest note, its reference frequency and the tuning offset in cents.

faq.title: Give me a creative idea
faq.answer: Use the calculator to tune a sustained drone to a song’s root note. Then slightly detune a second oscillator to create slow beating and movement.

faq.title: What does the cents value mean?
faq.answer: A cent is one hundredth of a semitone. A positive cents offset is sharper than the reference note; a negative offset is flatter.
keywords: what does the cents value mean?

faq.title: Can I convert a note back to hertz?
faq.answer: Use the note and frequency controls to look up the equal-tempered frequency of a pitch. The tool is a reference converter, not an audio tuner listening to a microphone.
keywords: can i convert a note back to hertz?

granular-pad.summary: Granular Pad splits audio into small overlapping grains to create stretched, scattered and evolving textures from a sound file.
granular-pad.capabilities: Granular Pad splits audio into small overlapping grains to create stretched, scattered and evolving textures from a sound file. Choose a question below for first steps, specific controls or a creative idea.

faq.title: What is Granular Pad?
faq.answer: Granular Pad splits audio into small overlapping grains to create stretched, scattered and evolving textures from a sound file.

faq.title: How do I start?
faq.answer: Import audio or load the demo. Try Soft Mist or Frozen Cloud, then adjust Grain Size, Density and Scan Speed while listening.

faq.title: Give me a creative idea
faq.answer: Freeze the scan around a vocal breath or piano tail, use a high Density and a little Pitch Scatter, then widen Stereo Spread for a suspended atmosphere.

faq.title: How can I freeze a sound?
faq.answer: Lower Scan Speed to zero and click the waveform to choose the grain scan position. Density controls the flow of grains while Grain Size changes their duration.
keywords: how can i freeze a sound?

faq.title: Can I export a granular texture?
faq.answer: Yes. Export renders a stereo 16-bit WAV using the granular engine. Very large files may take longer to process; the source input is limited to ten minutes.
keywords: can i export a granular texture?

hold-the-frequency.summary: Hold the Frequency is an interactive seven-stage tone ritual. Each stage asks you to sustain interaction with a glowing visual core.
hold-the-frequency.capabilities: Hold the Frequency is an interactive seven-stage tone ritual. Each stage asks you to sustain interaction with a glowing visual core. Choose a question below for first steps, specific controls or a creative idea.

faq.title: What is Hold the Frequency?
faq.answer: Hold the Frequency is an interactive seven-stage tone ritual. Each stage asks you to sustain interaction with a glowing visual core.
keywords: tell me about hold the frequency

faq.title: How do I start?
faq.answer: Enable audio if you want sound, then press and hold the glowing core. Maintain the hold for 60 uninterrupted seconds to complete the stage.

faq.title: Give me a creative idea
faq.answer: Treat each stage as a listening exercise: notice the sustained tone, the changing visuals and how your attention shifts while you keep the core held.

faq.title: What happens if I release early?
faq.answer: Releasing the glowing core before 60 seconds restarts the current stage. Finish the full hold to progress to the next of the seven stages.
keywords: what happens if i release early?

faq.title: Can I save my progress?
faq.answer: Yes. Save Progress stores your state locally in the browser. Restore loads that local state and Reset Session starts again.

kaleidoscope-studio.summary: Kaleidoscope Studio is a circular polyrhythm sequencer with four rhythmic voices and editable beat points.
kaleidoscope-studio.capabilities: Kaleidoscope Studio is a circular polyrhythm sequencer with four rhythmic voices and editable beat points. Choose a question below for first steps, specific controls or a creative idea.

faq.title: What is Kaleidoscope Studio?
faq.answer: Kaleidoscope Studio is a circular polyrhythm sequencer with four rhythmic voices and editable beat points.

faq.title: How do I start?
faq.answer: Choose a polyrhythm preset, press Play and move the beat points around the circular tracks. Change the voice sound, Pitch, Decay and Tone.

faq.title: Give me a creative idea
faq.answer: Start from a 3:4:5:7 rhythm. Give every ring a contrasting percussion sound, then mute one ring at a time to hear the hidden groove inside the cycle.

faq.title: How do the four rhythm rings work?
faq.answer: Each ring represents an independent rhythmic cycle with editable beat points. All rings run together, so different divisions produce repeating polyrhythmic alignments.
keywords: how do the four rhythm rings work?

faq.title: Can I change each percussion sound?
faq.answer: Yes. Each of the four voices has a sound choice and Pitch, Decay and Tone controls. Experiment with sharp attacks on one ring and softer tones on another.
keywords: can i change each percussion sound?

knot.summary: Knot is a playable browser synthesizer with oscillators, filters, envelopes, modulation, effects, scale tools and MIDI input.
knot.capabilities: Knot is a playable browser synthesizer with oscillators, filters, envelopes, modulation, effects, scale tools and MIDI input. Choose a question below for first steps, specific controls or a creative idea.

faq.title: What is Knot?
faq.answer: Knot is a playable browser synthesizer with oscillators, filters, envelopes, modulation, effects, scale tools and MIDI input.

faq.title: How do I start?
faq.answer: Choose a waveform or preset, shape the filter and envelope, then play notes with the on-screen keyboard or a supported MIDI controller.

faq.title: Give me a creative idea
faq.answer: Build a slowly moving pad: use a mellow oscillator tone, slower Attack and longer Release, then add gentle modulation and spatial effects. Record a sustained progression.

faq.title: What is Scale Quantize?
faq.answer: Scale Quantize maps incoming keyboard and MIDI notes to the notes of a selected scale. Multiple pressed keys may map to the same pitch.

faq.title: Can I record a WAV in Knot?

faq.title: What does Loudness Utility measure?

faq.answer: No. Loudness Utility applies uniform gain, not compression or limiting. If your requested loudness would exceed the chosen peak ceiling, the result stays below target.

faq.answer: It estimates integrated loudness, momentary and short-term loudness, and true peak. These are browser estimates, not certified broadcast measurements.

faq.answer: Import an audio file, Analyze, choose target and ceiling, Normalize, then Export WAV.

faq.answer: White noise has roughly equal power per hertz, pink noise rolls off toward higher frequencies and brown noise emphasizes lower frequencies even more.

faq.title: Give me a creative idea
faq.answer: Compare 3:4 and 5:7 at the same tempo. Tap along to just one layer, then shift your focus to the other and notice how the groove changes.

faq.title: How can I understand 3:4?
faq.answer: A 3:4 polyrhythm divides the same common span into three evenly spaced events against four. Follow the animations to hear when their accents align again.

faq.title: Can I adjust its sound?
faq.answer: Yes. Tone and Reverb controls change the synthesized rhythmic timbres. Try contrasting dry, sharp hits with a more spacious version.

faq.answer: For a distant ambient atmosphere, try Hall or Cathedral with a longer Decay. Lower the brightness using Damping and retain some dry signal for clarity.

faq.title: What does pre-delay do?
faq.answer: Pre-delay controls how long the direct sound plays before reverberation becomes prominent. A small gap can preserve transients even in a long reverb.

faq.title: How can I compare spaces?
faq.answer: Switch between Room, Chamber, Plate, Hall and Cathedral while keeping the input sound the same. Adjust Mix to compare each space at a similar wet level.

faq.title: How do I start?
faq.answer: Choose a Motion Seed, select Rising or Falling and press Play. Set Speed and Depth, then shape Brightness and Reverb.

faq.title: Give me a creative idea
faq.answer: Use a slow rising Shepard texture beneath a transition. Increase the sense of movement gradually, then cut the layer just before the downbeat to emphasize the arrival.

faq.title: What makes the tone feel endless?
faq.answer: Multiple sine tones glide across octaves while fading in and out at different ranges. The blend creates a rising or falling impression without a final high or low note.
keywords: what makes the tone feel endless?

faq.title: How do I record a WAV?
faq.answer: Press Record, let the tone evolve and stop recording to capture the master audio as WAV. Recording relies on compatible browser media capture and decoding.
keywords: how do i record a wav?

faq.title: How do I shape the sound?
faq.answer: Adjust Speed for movement, Octave Depth for range, and Speed Warp for variation. Use Tone/Brightness and Reverb to shape the texture, or start with a motion preset.

faq.title: What do Rising and Falling mean?
faq.answer: Rising makes the sound seem to climb forever; Falling makes it seem to descend forever. Layered tones fade in and out to create the illusion.

faq.title: What is a Shepard tone?
faq.answer: A Shepard tone is an auditory illusion. Several octave-spaced tones rise or fall together as their volumes shift, creating the impression of an endless ascent or descent.

faq.title: How do I start the sound?
faq.answer: Click Play to start Shepard. If you hear nothing, check your audio output and volume, then click Play again. Browsers may block audio until you interact with the page.

faq.answer: Threshold sets the level at which compression begins. Ratio controls strength, Attack and Release control timing, and Makeup changes output gain.

faq.title: What is Musical MIDI?
faq.answer: Musical MIDI exports note events from editable 16-step patterns, with markers and instrument tracks.

faq.title: Can I save a project?

faq.answer: Use Space on a short vocal phrase, increase the wet mix for a floating tail, then try Robot on a duplicate to create a contrasting synthetic layer.

faq.answer: Doubler thickens the source; Pitch shifts pitch; Robot adds mechanical coloration; Space adds delay and reverb. Character changes the behavior within the chosen mode.

faq.title: What does Robot do?
faq.answer: Robot combines moving filtering, distortion and harmonic processing. It also works as a creative effect on instrumental melodies.
